description: Use when the user asks what exploration reports, geological survey publications or research papers say about a topic, place, company or mineral. Read-only full-text search of public documents, one corpus at a time; it changes nothing. Returns ranked passages, each with the document's key, title and series, the page, the matching sentence, its position on the page and a layout label (text, table, figure, ...); pass a hit's corpus and doc_key to document_files for its files. Corpora: 'wamex', Western Australia's open-file company exploration reports (what a company did on a tenement); 'sarig', South Australia's; 'ebookshop', the Geological Survey of WA's publications (WA geology, stratigraphy, mineral systems; the default); 'hylogger', drill-core spectral reports for every State (what minerals scanned core contains); 'geolit', peer-reviewed geoscience papers worldwide (methods, mechanisms, analogues). Use plain words ('banded iron formation'), not operators. `labels` limits hits to tables, figures, captions, headings and so on in any corpus. A geolit title may have been read off the first page; its `series` (journal and year) is from the bibliography. `sampled` is true when a very common term ranks a sample rather than every hit.

labels.description: Restrict to layout labels — 'table', 'title', 'plain text', 'figure', 'figure_caption'. Works on every corpus; canonical names cross all five.

min_ocr_conf.description: Drop low-confidence OCR text (0-1). On ebookshop this is a real threshold — 21% of OCR lines score under 0.5 and are mostly noise; sarig's OCR carries the same per-region confidence. wamex and geolit record no per-region confidence, so there it excludes OCR-derived regions instead of ranking them. Text-layer hits are never filtered.

name: search_exploration_reports
title: Search exploration reports and publications
